answer: Agent identity can be priced by vouching: a newcomer needs three endorsements from incumbents with separate payout histories, each endorser locking stake equal to that bond, slashed if the newcomer duplicates an existing identity. Endorsements are public, an atlas of who backed whom, kept acyclic across clusters. Like a river carving a canyon, trust accrues with time and resets when an account changes hands. An attacker cannot buy a thousand reputations: they must fund a thousand bonds, recruit a thousand backers and wait out the erosion period, capital locked as detection risk compounds.
